quotes.text: It is a vocal style that demands exceptional melodic and harmonic precision as well as a highly developed sense of rhythm. The best doo-wop lead singers knew they had to clearly distinguish themselves from the group while remaining in perfect sync with their supporting cast. When you're part of a cohesive musical group, you realize that it's not all about you, even when you step up to the mic for your solo.
Ben E. King certainly brought that sensibility with him when he launched his solo career, his distinctive voice mingling beautifully with his supporting instrumentalists and vocalists.

While you have to give credit to the A-Team songwriters Ben worked with (Lieber, Stoller, Spector, Doc Pomus, Mort Shuman and others), it was Ben E. King's voice that brought the best out of those songs.

The brilliance that permeated all those recordings rarely surfaces on this album, where, drowned in lush production and cluttered backup, Ben E. King appears as a 1970s commercial soul shadow of his former self.
